title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page characterises 'limited' (bounded) subsets M of K(X), X projective. Three equivalent conditions are given: (i) M lies among the differences γ(F_i) − γ(G_i) for bounded families of locally free sheaves; (ii) the same, with F and G locally free quotients of O(−n)^N whose Hilbert polynomials lie in a finite set; (iii) there is a fixed A such that ξ + γ(A) is represented by locally free quotients of O(−n)^N. These are proved by the usual characterisation of bounded families (Hilbert/Quot schemes).

This page passes to cycles. X is projective and smooth, and M' is a subgroup or subset of Z^i(X), the codimension-i cycles, considered up to some adequate equivalence. The transcription reads 'K-équivalence'; the image could also be read as algebraic or rational equivalence. Grothendieck lists candidate conditions, apparently intended to be equivalent or compared:
(i) M' is limited, i.e. its elements are given by a bounded family of algebraic cycles: finitely many components of Chow/Hilbert schemes, taking differences.
(ii) M' is 'numerically limited', i.e. its numerical classes form a bounded (finite) set. In addition there is a real class ξ0 (written in Z^1(X)⊗R, more naturally in Z^i(X)⊗R) such that every ξ0 + ξ, for ξ in M', is 'positive', i.e. a limit of positive (effective) cycles. Modern reading: a uniform pseudo-effectivity shift.
(iii) There is a bounded family M ⊂ K(X) such that each ξ in M' satisfies (i−1)!·ξ = c^i(x) for some x in M. This uses Riemann–Roch without denominators: c_i(O_Z) = (−1)^{i−1}(i−1)!·[Z] for Z of codimension i. So boundedness of cycles is transferred to boundedness in K-theory, up to the factor (i−1)!.
(iv) There is a bounded M ⊂ K^{(i)}(X), the filtration by codimension of support, with M' contained in its image under K^{(i)} → gr^i K ≅ (cycles mod equivalence, up to torsion).
(v) M' is numerically limited. This is the bare condition, without positivity.

Purpose: to formulate a boundedness theory for algebraic cycles in arbitrary codimension, parallel to the theory for divisors. That divisor theory is the Matsusaka / Kleiman finiteness theorems for the Picard functor, numerical boundedness and ampleness. Its use is in finiteness questions around the standard conjectures, e.g. finiteness of cycle groups modulo equivalence and comparison of algebraic and numerical equivalence. The page is a list of conditions with no proofs. Several implications are obvious: (i) ⇒ (iv) ⇒ (iii) up to the factor, using Hilbert schemes and resolutions; (i) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (v). The reverse implications are the real conjectural content.
errors: The conditions are only listed; no implications are proved on this page.

The reverse implication 'numerically limited (v) ⇒ limited (i)' is false if cycles are taken modulo algebraic equivalence. Griffiths (1969) and Clemens (1983, infinitely generated Griffiths group) give infinitely many homologically trivial cycles that are pairwise algebraically inequivalent. Such a set is numerically limited (a single numerical class, positivity condition easily satisfied) but cannot come from a bounded family modulo algebraic equivalence. So any equivalence (v) ⇔ (i) can only hold for numerical (or homological-type) equivalence. Even then (ii) is needed, since positivity is required in codimension 1 for Matsusaka-type statements.
ξ0 is written in Z^1(X)⊗R. For cycles of codimension i the shift should presumably lie in Z^i(X)⊗R, unless it is meant as ξ0^i or a degree-type condition; this is probably a slip.
The sign (−1)^{i−1} in the Riemann–Roch-without-denominators formula is omitted; this is harmless for boundedness.
Condition (iii) as transcribed reads '∃ ξ ∈ M ... (i−1)!ξ = c^i(ξ)'. Two different letters are needed: an element x of K(X) and a cycle ξ in M'.

ideas.what: Notion of a 'limited' (bounded) subset of K(X) via bounded families of locally free sheaves (previous page), transported to cycles
ideas.modern_name: bounded families of sheaves / cycles (Quot, Hilbert, Chow schemes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (FGA, Hilbert schemes); Kleiman (SGA 6 Exp. XIII)
ideas.where_published: FGA (Techniques de construction IV); SGA 6 Exp. XIII (Kleiman, finiteness theorems)

ideas.what: Transferring boundedness of codimension-i cycles to boundedness in K-theory through (i−1)!·[Z] = ±c_i(O_Z)
ideas.modern_name: Riemann–Roch without denominators applied to boundedness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jouanolou / Grothendieck (RR without denominators, SGA 6 Exp. XIV)
ideas.where_published: Riemann–Roch without denominators is in SGA 6; its use as a boundedness criterion for cycles is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Numerical boundedness plus a uniform positivity shift (ξ0 + ξ a limit of effective cycles) as a criterion for boundedness of a family of cycles in any codimension
ideas.modern_name: higher-codimension analogue of Matsusaka/Kleiman numerical boundedness; pseudo-effective cones of cycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Matsusaka, Kleiman (divisors); higher codimension cones: Fulger–Lehmann, Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin (2010s)
ideas.where_published: related questions appear in Kleiman's exposition of the standard conjectures; exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Using the codimension filtration K^{(i)}(X) and its map to cycles to define boundedness of cycle sets
ideas.modern_name: topological (coniveau) filtration on K_0 and gr^i K vs CH^i

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a boundedness programme for codimension-i cycles. The candidate equivalence is that 'numerically limited + uniformly pseudo-effective after a fixed shift' should mean 'coming from a bounded family of cycles', checked through K-theory via Riemann–Roch without denominators. The question is left open on this page.
missed.quote: Les familles de M' sont "numériquement limitées" ... et ∃ classe ξ0 ... ξ0 + ξ (ξ ∈ M) soient "positifs" i.e. limite par des cycles positifs.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Boundedness of effective cycles with bounded numerical class in higher codimension relates to the modern study of pseudo-effective cones of higher-codimension cycles, which behave unexpectedly (Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin; Fulger–Lehmann). Griffiths/Clemens show the statement fails modulo algebraic equivalence. The precise form Grothendieck intended, with the K-theoretic criterion, may be a modest historical precursor. It is unlikely to be new mathematics.

missed.claim: Boundedness of cycles is linked to boundedness in K_0 through the integrality factor (i−1)! from Riemann–Roch without denominators.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a K-theoretic (Hilbert/Quot-scheme) route to finiteness statements for cycle groups. It is a natural idea, but I know of no explicit published treatment attributed to Grothendieck.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a sketchy list of candidate conditions for boundedness of cycle families: a natural extension of the divisor theory (SGA 6 Exp. XIII) with a K-theory twist. It is interesting as a trace of Grothendieck's thinking on finiteness around the standard conjectures, but nothing is proved. The naive equivalence modulo algebraic equivalence is refuted by Griffiths' example.
transcription_corrections: Condition (i) likely reads: 'La famille M' est limitée, i.e. définie par une famille limitée de cycles algébriques' (not 'Si la famille ... elle définie').
In (iii) it should read '∃ x ∈ M tel que (i−1)! ξ = c^i(x)' for each ξ ∈ M'; the element of K(X) is distinct from the cycle ξ.
In (ii) the parenthetical '(ξ ∈ M)' should be '(ξ ∈ M')'.
'cycles à K-équivalence près' is an uncertain reading; it could be 'à équivalence ... près' with an unclear qualifier.
'sous-groupe' (or 'partie') M' of Z^i(X); in (iv) the target is K^{(i)}(X), with M' ⊂ 'Image de M'.
